question: Can a differentiable network of probabilistically interpreted AND, OR, and NOT concepts learn accurate tabular classifiers while yielding compact, directly readable IF-THEN rules, including when relevant variables or feature values are unobserved?

key_findings.claim: The paper gives Neural Logic Network edges a signed probabilistic interpretation that represents either a concept or its negation with one parameter.
key_findings.evidence: For an AND node, a positive edge is the modeled probability that the source concept is necessary and a negative edge is minus the probability that its complement is necessary; OR edges analogously model sufficient concepts. The construction assumes that the concept and its negation cannot simultaneously have nonzero roles, creating a signed one-dimensional search path between contradictory hypotheses.

key_findings.claim: AND and OR biases summarize residual activation attributed to unobserved concepts, but they do not identify any latent variable or its semantics.
key_findings.evidence: The AND bias is the conditional probability that all unobserved necessary concepts hold when the observed definition holds; the OR bias is the probability that some unobserved sufficient concept holds when no observed sufficient concept holds. In the implementation each entire latent set is compressed to one scalar, then re-estimated from empirical rule coverage after training. Calling this an account of unobserved data is valid as residual probability modeling, not as latent-concept discovery.

anchors.section: Dataset coverage analysis and bias adjustment

key_findings.claim: The tractable probabilistic forward pass depends on three independence assumptions, and the paper explicitly concedes that the third is false in most nontrivial networks.
key_findings.evidence: The first assumption separates concept presence from its higher-layer necessary or sufficient role; the second treats distinct structural roles as independent; the third assumes conditional independence of concepts in the same layer given the input. Shared ancestors violate the third assumption unless the circuit is decomposable. The exact dependence-aware alternative requires joint tensors with exponentially many entries, so the practical method retains the approximation.

key_findings.claim: The probabilistic equations are exactly logical only in a narrow binary, integer-weight, full-observation limit.
key_findings.evidence: When inputs are binary, weights are in {-1,0,1}, AND biases equal one, and OR biases equal zero, the product formulas coincide with classical logic and need none of the probabilistic independence assumptions. Continuous fuzzy dichotomies, nonbinary missing-value weights, and nonbinary residual biases move the deployed model outside this exact regime even after structural weights are discretized.

key_findings.claim: The model's readable output is enforced by a two-layer DNF architecture with feature-specific preprocessing and factorized rule modules.
key_findings.evidence: A hidden AND layer with allowed negation feeds a non-negated OR output layer, so each class is a disjunction of conjunctive rules. Categorical modules learn OR equivalence classes; continuous modules learn sigmoid thresholds, AND intervals, and OR collections of intervals. Each rule gets its own categorical and continuous representation while sharing one-hot and fuzzy-threshold encodings, reducing parameter coupling and making final rules expressible in original feature terms.

key_findings.claim: Interpretability is produced by a substantial post-training search pipeline rather than by gradient learning alone.
key_findings.evidence: After Adam training with L2, non-empty, and L1 penalties, the method greedily discretizes every structural edge using full-training-set loss, retrains the continuous biases and threshold parameters, repeatedly prunes any edge that does not worsen loss, recalibrates biases by coverage, and removes coverage-included rules. The selected descending discretizer requires O(number of weights times dataset size) evaluations and is named by the authors as a severe runtime limitation.

key_findings.claim: The epoch-wise dead-rule reset is a plausible optimization device but empirically contributes at most a marginal gain.
key_findings.evidence: Dead rules have their definitions randomly reinitialized and outgoing weights zeroed after every epoch so they can search new clauses without changing current predictions. Across ten seeds on five selected datasets, reset improves average F1 systematically but by no more than 0.25 percentage points, while seed standard deviations are often larger than configuration differences. The paper itself questions whether reset is useful.

key_findings.claim: On four complete Boolean-network truth-table tasks, NLN reports the strongest predictive results and recovers equivalent compact programs from partial samples.
key_findings.evidence: With 16% of each truth table, five-fold accuracy exceeds 97% on all four networks; at 40% it is 100% throughout, while NN-LFIT, D-LFIT, LF1T, and JRip remain below 100% or time out. Appendix examples show exact, subsumed, or resolution-equivalent rules, and also show how insufficient data can merge two true clauses into one overgeneral rule. The aggregate table reports predictive accuracy, not a formal rule-equivalence score across all repetitions.

key_findings.claim: On ordinary tabular data, compactness comes with large predictive losses whenever the target is not naturally a small DNF.
key_findings.evidence: Across eight UCI variants, NLN matches RRL closely on tic-tac-toe, chess, kidney, and wine but scores 79.22 versus 95.26 on Monk2, 65.38 versus 80.31 on Adult, 57.54 versus 73.86 on continuous Balance, and 53.75 versus 78.84 on categorical Balance. XGBoost also exceeds NLN on six of eight rows. The authors attribute the gap to rigid readable structure and acknowledge that their current learning strategy is generally insufficient outside ground-truth logic programs.

key_findings.claim: NLN can recover much smaller rule sets than RRL, but the comparison conflates different output semantics and lacks human interpretability evaluation.
key_findings.evidence: For tic-tac-toe, NLN recovers eight size-three rules versus 313.6 RRL rules on average; for chess and kidney it also uses far fewer clauses. Yet RRL combines small hidden rules with a learned linear output, so treating each hidden node as an independent final rule overstates its human-facing rule count. Rule number and average literal count are the only interpretability measures; no domain-expert comprehension, fidelity, stability, or task-time study is reported.

key_findings.claim: The four-rule kidney model is an exploratory full-dataset fit, not a clinically validated diagnostic rule set.
key_findings.evidence: Five cross-validation models are merged, repruned on all 400 records, and searched for a four-rule subset that classifies the same complete dataset perfectly. One selected rule is simply diabetes_mellitus=yes implies CKD. The authors correctly warn that the small dataset and stochastic rule search make perfect fit no proof of truth, but no held-out hospital, temporal cohort, calibration, subgroup, clinician, or uncertainty validation follows.

key_findings.claim: The cybersecurity case demonstrates readable transfer but exposes a substantial unseen-distribution weakness.
key_findings.evidence: A 24-rule binary NLN scores 99.73 F1 on NSL-KDD training and 81.37 on its test set, below LAD's 84.78 test score despite higher training score. Reassigning and pruning the rules for five classes yields 88.97 training F1 but only 60.86 test F1 because the test set includes 16 unseen attack types and much more U2R/R2L. No modern tree, RRL, DLN, RNS, or neural baseline is reported in this application.

key_findings.claim: The model learns observational decision rules and cannot support the paper's occasional language of discovering an underlying causal structure.
key_findings.evidence: Section 2.4 explicitly states that the same AND or OR node admits multiple causal directions and structures and that interpretation requires external expert knowledge. The loss fits P(Y|x) from observational rows, with no intervention, temporal ordering, instruments, invariance assumptions, or causal identification theorem. The resulting rules can reveal associations or candidate mechanisms, not uniquely recover causes.

method.core_idea: Build the classifier itself as a soft probabilistic DNF whose signed edges choose positive or negated concepts, then turn the trained soft network into a compact discrete program through greedy discretization, continuous-parameter refitting, pruning, and empirical bias calibration.
method.mechanism: Input concepts are binary probabilities. Categorical values are one-hot encoded and grouped into learned OR equivalence classes; continuous features pass through learned sigmoid thresholds that form intervals and unions of intervals. Each factorized module produces one AND clause with optional negative literals and a scalar residual bias. An OR output gathers clauses for each class. Product t-norm/t-conorm equations provide differentiable forward values under independence assumptions. Adam minimizes squared label error plus non-empty and sparsity penalties, while dead clauses are reset each epoch. Post-training, structural weights are greedily set to their sign or zero based on full-training loss; biases, bounds, sharpness, and missing-value probabilities are retrained; unnecessary parameters and coverage-redundant clauses are removed; and rule/output biases are recomputed from covered probability mass.
assumptions: Presence of a concept in a realization is independent of every source concept's general necessary or sufficient role in the next layer.
Distinct necessary or sufficient roles entering one node are mutually independent except for the explicitly paired concept and its negation.
Concepts within a layer are conditionally independent given the observed input even when they share ancestors; this known-false approximation prevents exponential inference.
For each edge, a source concept and its negation cannot both have nonzero structural probability, so one signed scalar can represent both hypotheses.
A scalar residual activation probability is an adequate summary of all relevant but unobserved necessary or sufficient concepts.
A two-layer DNF is a suitable human-readable target representation even when an equivalent CNF or arithmetic relation is much smaller.
L2 fitting of binary labels provides useful probability estimates, although proper calibration is not evaluated.
Greedy one-edge-at-a-time discretization and pruning find a useful discrete program from the continuous optimum.
Rule count and literal-equivalent size are adequate proxies for actual human interpretability.
Five-fold results on selected small UCI datasets and one legacy intrusion benchmark characterize practical tabular performance.

techniques.role: Represents a concept or its negation as mutually exclusive necessary or sufficient roles with one signed weight.
Summarizes activation due to unobserved necessary or sufficient concepts with one scalar per node.
Uses product t-norm, probabilistic-sum t-conorm, and strong negation for differentiable AND/OR/NOT propagation.
Restricts class decisions to ORs of independently learned AND rule modules.
Learns sigmoid thresholds, intervals, and unions of intervals for readable continuous-feature conditions.
Reinitializes dead clauses while zeroing their outgoing edges so ongoing predictions remain unchanged.
Converts each soft structural edge to zero or its sign using full-training-set loss.
Refits residual rule and output biases from empirical covered probability mass and removes included rules.
Concatenates rules learned in separate folds and reprunes them into one program.
Copies binary anomaly rules across multiclass outputs, then reprunes and recalibrates without gradient retraining.

evaluations.setting: Four Boolean gene-network truth tables with 8%, 16%, 40%, or 80% of all state transitions
evaluations.metric: Two repeats of five-fold cross-validation accuracy and qualitative ground-truth rule recovery
evaluations.result: At 16%, NLN scores 98.46, 97.69, 99.57, and 100%; at 40% it scores 100% on all four networks.
evaluations.baseline: NN-LFIT, D-LFIT, LF1T, and JRip; several symbolic/extraction methods time out on the two larger state spaces

evaluations.setting: Eight UCI tabular variants under five-fold cross-validation
evaluations.result: NLN: 100 tic-tac-toe, 99.31 chess, 79.22 Monk2, 98.08 kidney, 94.44 wine, 65.38 Adult, 57.54 continuous Balance, 53.75 categorical Balance.

evaluations.setting: Rule-complexity comparison on the eight UCI variants
evaluations.metric: Average rule count and literal-equivalent rule size
evaluations.result: NLN exactly recovers about 8 size-3 tic-tac-toe rules and uses 6.8 rules of average size 2.49 on kidney; Adult and Balance require 69-94 larger rules.
evaluations.baseline: RRL uses 313.6 tic-tac-toe rules and 35 kidney rules but smaller hidden rule size; ODD usually uses fewer clauses on non-logical targets

evaluations.setting: Known ground-truth rule audit on tic-tac-toe and Monk2
evaluations.metric: Recovered rule fraction and excess-rule proportion
evaluations.result: NLN recovers 100% of tic-tac-toe with 0% excess and 53.3% of Monk2 with 24% excess.
evaluations.baseline: RRL recovers 75%/0% with 3820%/573.33% excess; ODD recovers 0%/20% with 360%/86.7% excess

evaluations.setting: Merged chronic-kidney-disease classifier on all 400 UCI records
evaluations.result: Four selected clauses fit all records perfectly; two clauses reach 98.99% F1.
evaluations.baseline: Merged RRL needs 13 distinct nonempty displayed rules for perfect full-dataset fit

evaluations.setting: NSL-KDD binary attack detection with 23 training attack types and 16 additional test-only attack types
evaluations.result: 24-rule NLN scores 99.73 training, 81.37 test, and 96.94 on concatenated data.
evaluations.baseline: 37-rule LAD scores 95.94 training, 84.78 test, and 94.25 concatenated

evaluations.setting: Direct transfer of binary NSL-KDD clauses to five-way attack classification
evaluations.result: After copying, repruning, and bias adjustment, 17 rules score 88.97 training, 60.86 test, and 84.70 concatenated without multiclass gradient training.
evaluations.baseline: No learned multiclass baseline is reported

evaluations.setting: Discretization and rule-reset ablation on five selected datasets with ten seeds each
evaluations.metric: Mean and seed standard deviation of five-fold F1
evaluations.result: Greedy discretizers improve about 0.5-1.5 points on average over thresholding; additive is best overall. Reset improves at most 0.25 points and effects are commonly smaller than seed variation.
evaluations.baseline: No discretization, 0.5 thresholding, four greedy discretizers, and no-reset variants

limitations: Author-stated: same-layer conditional independence is false in most useful NLNs; exact inference has exponential time and memory in layer widths.
Author-stated: vanishing gradients make NLNs difficult to train and the reset scheme is not enough to learn good predictive models in general.
Author-stated: greedy discretization requires O(w times |D|) model evaluations and is a severe runtime bottleneck.
Author-stated: DNF rules are a poor representation for arithmetic comparison tasks such as Balance unless nearly every case is enumerated.
Author-stated: stochastic initialization can yield different but prediction-equivalent rule sets, giving users different interpretations of the same data.
Reviewer-identified: no theorem establishes statistical consistency, rule-identification conditions, generalization, calibration, or approximation error under violated independence assumptions.
Reviewer-identified: residual biases do not reveal which variables are missing and can absorb misspecification, label noise, or selection bias while being narrated as unobserved concepts.
Reviewer-identified: the single signed edge forbids simultaneously considering a concept and its negation as distinct probabilistic roles and creates a zero-weight optimization barrier between them.
Reviewer-identified: exact classical-logic semantics disappear with nonbinary biases, fuzzy boundaries, and missing-value probabilities, even after edges are discretized.

Reviewer-identified: the tabular benchmark contains only eight legacy UCI variants and omits modern multi-dataset suites, recent DLN/RNS methods, calibrated rule lists, GAMs, and foundation-model baselines.
Reviewer-identified: most main comparison tables provide no seed uncertainty or statistical tests; only the late ablation reports ten-seed variability on five favorable datasets.
Reviewer-identified: the F1 averaging convention and threshold-selection split for multiclass, multilabel, and imbalanced tasks are not specified clearly enough for exact reproduction.

Reviewer-identified: rule count and literal count are structural proxies; no human comprehension, simulation, trust calibration, editing, or expert-validity evaluation supports the interpretability claim.
Reviewer-identified: comparing NLN output clauses with every RRL hidden rule is not semantically matched because RRL's decision is a weighted linear combination of those nodes.
Reviewer-identified: the Boolean comparison partially reproduces prior reported numbers and timeouts rather than presenting matched implementations, budgets, seeds, and hardware runtimes.
Reviewer-identified: five-fold accuracy on a sampled fraction of a truth table is not by itself proof of logical equivalence on every unsampled state; aggregate exact-rule recovery is not reported.
Reviewer-identified: the medical four-rule subset is chosen and evaluated on the same 400 rows after merging all folds, so perfect fit is descriptive and highly selection-adapted.
Reviewer-identified: the NSL-KDD test result is weaker than LAD and the multiclass transfer falls to 60.86 F1, with no modern comparator or repeated-seed interval.
Reviewer-identified: the paper sometimes calls observational rule learning causal-structure discovery despite explicitly acknowledging non-identifiability of causal direction.
Reviewer-identified: missingness probabilities can learn dataset-specific missing-not-at-random patterns that fail or encode sensitive workflow artifacts under deployment shift.
failure_modes: Multiplying many soft inputs drives AND activations and gradients toward zero, killing clauses before they discover useful combinations.
Reset rules repeatedly sample the same unproductive region while seed choice dominates configuration gains.
Greedy edge discretization locks in an early local choice that blocks a better jointly discrete program.
A target has a short CNF or arithmetic rule but an exponentially large DNF, producing many clauses or poor accuracy.
Two same-layer concepts share ancestors; independence multiplication double-counts evidence and yields miscalibrated outputs.
Residual biases fit label prevalence and hide a wrong observed definition, making an apparently probabilistic rule hard to falsify.
Continuous fuzzy thresholds leave duplicate near-identical clauses that coverage pruning cannot recognize as included.
Rule count appears low only because one module contains a large union of categorical values or many disjoint continuous intervals.
A high-performing but spurious rule such as diabetes implies kidney disease fits a small cohort and is mistaken for clinical knowledge.
Missing-value weights exploit institution-specific measurement or documentation behavior and fail at another site.
Rules differ across seeds, so downstream experts receive incompatible narratives despite similar predictive scores.
Binary anomaly clauses bind to seen attack families and collapse on unseen multiclass categories.
Perfect partial-truth-table accuracy masks incorrect behavior on unobserved Boolean assignments.
Post-processing on all available development data overfits structural choices, thresholds, and biases before deployment.
open_questions: Can an exact or bounded-error tractable circuit constraint replace the known-false same-layer independence approximation?
Can joint discrete optimization, differentiable SAT, or straight-through selectors remove the O(w|D|) greedy discretization pass?
When is a rule program identifiable up to Boolean equivalence from partial truth tables, and can exact recovery probability be bounded?
Can the architecture select between DNF, CNF, decision lists, and arithmetic predicates according to description length?
How calibrated are rule and output biases under class imbalance, missingness, and violated structural assumptions?
Can explicit latent-variable modules discover named unobserved concepts rather than compressing them into residual probabilities?
Do learned rules remain stable under bootstrap resampling, seed changes, temporal shift, and site shift?
Which human-centered metrics predict whether clinicians or operators actually understand, audit, and safely edit the rules?
How does NLN compare with RNS, DLN, RRL, MINTY, TabLog, and modern sparse rule-list methods on a common large benchmark at matched complexity?
Can coverage pruning use formal logical implication or interval-set containment instead of a fuzzy empirical co-activation heuristic?
Can causal discovery assumptions such as interventions, temporal invariance, or multi-environment data be added without losing transparent rules?
How should sensitive or discriminatory literals be constrained, audited, and reported without treating transparency itself as fairness?
reusable_insights: Separate rule semantics, probability calibration, and causal interpretation; readable IF-THEN syntax alone guarantees none of the latter two.
Audit logic learners before and after discretization because the human-facing model can differ materially from the trained soft network.
Report rule stability across seeds and data resamples alongside average rule count; unstable explanations are not reliably actionable.
Use complete unsampled truth-table evaluation and Boolean-equivalence checking when the ground-truth program is known.
Benchmark DNF learners on targets with compact DNF, compact CNF, compact arithmetic form, and no compact symbolic form to expose representation bias.
Treat residual rule bias as a falsifiable calibration parameter, not evidence that a particular latent cause exists.
Measure the complexity inside each clause, including category-set size and number of continuous intervals, rather than counting modules only.
For high-stakes rules, require external cohort validation, calibration, subgroup analysis, and domain-expert review before interpreting full-dataset fit.
Missingness handling should be stress-tested under changed measurement policy because missing-value predictors often encode workflow rather than physiology.
Compare predictive accuracy at matched description length and human task performance, not only at each method's default model size.
Use exact circuit structure where possible; if an independence approximation is unavoidable, quantify its output and calibration error directly.
Rule merging and transfer are useful modular operations, but must retain independent held-out evaluation after every structural selection step.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpretable Classification via a Rule Network with Selective Logical Operators
competitive_landscape.difference: RNS lets each logical neuron select AND or OR with hard selectors, a negation layer, structural connection constraints, and straight-through gradient updates. Its current 2026 revision evaluates 13 datasets against 25 alternatives and explicitly targets gradient vanishing, rule quality, and efficiency. It threatens NLN's practical rule-learning novelty because it learns DNF or CNF structure rather than fixing DNF and avoids the expensive per-edge post hoc search; NLN remains distinct in its probabilistic signed-edge formalism, residual unobserved-data biases, missing-value probabilities, and rule calibration.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Interpretable Differentiable Logic Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: DLN relaxes binary logic operators, binarized inputs, and discrete connections for gradient training, reports 20 classification tasks, and emphasizes up to thousand-fold fewer gate operations than conventional neural networks. Its newer regression and time-series extensions broaden the platform further. NLN offers more explicit original-feature DNF clauses, fuzzy intervals, residual biases, and Boolean-network discovery, but does not report inference cost or comparable breadth.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Interpretable Rules for Scalable Data Representation and Classification
competitive_landscape.relationship: closest predecessor and strongest in-paper baseline
competitive_landscape.difference: RRL uses gradient grafting to optimize a discrete multilayer logical representation and demonstrates ten small plus four large datasets with an explicit accuracy-complexity tradeoff. NLN's main advance over RRL is fewer directly class-linked DNF clauses, signed negation, latent-information biases, natural missing values, and feature-specific rule modules. Its own Table 3 nevertheless shows RRL ahead by 15-25 F1 points on several non-logical tasks, and NLN's rule-count advantage partly reflects removing RRL's linear output semantics.

competitive_landscape.title: Disentangling Neural Disjunctive Normal Form Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: concurrent direct post-processing competitor from overlapping authors
competitive_landscape.difference: Baugh et al. target the same soft-to-symbolic bottleneck, showing that naive thresholding entangles nested rules and splitting nodes better preserves pre-translation performance across binary, multiclass, multilabel, and predicate-invention tasks. This directly competes with NLN's greedy discretization and pruning contribution: future work must compare accuracy retention, clause size, and cost against disentanglement rather than thresholding alone.

competitive_landscape.title: MINTY: Rule-based models that minimize the need for imputing features with missing values
competitive_landscape.difference: MINTY learns sparse rule disjunctions whose variables substitute for one another when features are missing and explicitly optimizes the fit-interpretability-missingness tradeoff. NLN instead learns a per-rule probability that a missing value belonged to the selected set, which can use informative missingness but may depend more strongly on deployment workflow. MINTY is therefore a necessary baseline for NLN's natural missing-value claim.

competitive_landscape.title: TabLog: Test-Time Adaptation for Tabular Data Using Logic Rules
competitive_landscape.difference: TabLog assumes logical structure is invariant but adapts numerical rule parameters and weights from unlabeled target data under distribution shift. NLN reports a manual binary-to-multiclass reprune-and-recalibrate transfer but no unlabeled adaptation objective or modern shift benchmark. TabLog narrows the novelty of rule transfer and exposes a missing robustness axis in the medical and intrusion applications.

competitive_landscape.title: Neurosymbolic Association Rule Mining from Tabular Data
competitive_landscape.difference: Aerial+ uses an undercomplete autoencoder and reconstruction-based symbolic extraction to obtain concise association rules with full coverage, and reports downstream runtime improvements over seven baselines. It is unsupervised association mining rather than direct class-rule learning, but directly addresses rule explosion and extraction scalability—the two weaknesses that dominate NLN's Adult, Balance, and discretization results.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims the first rigorous logical and probabilistic formalization of Neural Logic Network AND/OR nodes, signed NOT-capable weights, biases for unobserved data, factorized IF-THEN modules for mixed tabular features, a dead-rule reset plus discrete simplification pipeline, state-of-the-art Boolean-network discovery, and useful interpretable medical and industrial rules.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The formal derivation is a real contribution: it separates aleatoric concept presence from epistemic structural roles, states three assumptions instead of hiding them inside fuzzy operators, adds a coherent residual-bias interpretation, proves De Morgan compatibility, and shows why exact dependence-aware inference is exponential. The engineering pipeline also integrates categorical equivalence classes, continuous interval unions, missing-value probabilities, greedy discretization, calibration, pruning, fold-model merging, and rule transfer in one readable DNF system. Boolean truth-table results and exact tic-tac-toe recovery are strong within the chosen benchmark. However, most components sit in a crowded line spanning RRL, DLN, neural DNF, probabilistic circuits, and optimal rule methods. RNS now learns operator and normal-form structure with stronger breadth; concurrent disentanglement directly improves soft-to-symbolic translation; MINTY and TabLog cover missingness and shift more explicitly. NLN's ordinary tabular accuracy is often far below RRL, the reset effect is negligible, discretization is expensive, and the high-stakes examples are not externally validated.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The durable novelty is not generic interpretable classification or rule discovery. It is the unusually explicit probabilistic semantics for signed necessary/sufficient roles and residual unseen information, combined with an end-to-end human-readable mixed-feature DNF pipeline. A high-value extension should turn those semantics into measurable benefits: calibration under missingness, exact or bounded dependence handling, stable rule recovery, and auditable uncertainty. It should compare to RNS, DLN, RRL, neural-DNF disentanglement, MINTY, and TabLog on modern benchmarks at matched description length, report compute and stability, and avoid causal claims unless interventions or multi-environment identification are added.

reviewer_notes: Complete primary pass: all 60 extracted pages were read end to end, including the main 26-page TMLR article, references, notation, full AND/OR probability derivations, the dependence-aware exponential alternative, De Morgan proofs, causal-interpretation examples, all four discretizers, coverage-inclusion heuristic, Boolean truth-table protocol and rule listings, medical merge details, all 24 NSL-KDD rules, and ten-seed ablations. Rendered pages 4, 5, 13, 15, 16, 20-22, 24-25, 42, 48, and 60 were inspected at original detail to verify architecture diagrams, tables, learned clinical rules, class-coverage plots, independence experiment, Boolean results, and seed variability. Current competition was checked through primary arXiv, PMLR proceedings, and OpenReview routes as of 2026-08-23, including RNS, DLN, RRL, neural-DNF disentanglement, MINTY, TabLog, Aerial+, and NEUROLOGIC. The extracted source is arXiv v6, revised 2026-06-26 and journal-referenced as TMLR June 2026.
